slides.title: 51WORLD Unveils Two Embodied AI Products
slides.highlight: The introduction of new embodied AI products is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

slides.title: LF AI & Data Foundation Welcomes AIRSEAI to Unite Open Source Embodied AI Ecosystem
slides.highlight: The integration of AIRSEAI into the LF AI & Data Foundation supports the development of an open source embodied AI ecosystem, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: TurnBench: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Turn-Taking Dynamics in Spoken Dialogue
slides.highlight: This work introduces TurnBench, a benchmark for end-of-turn and interruption detection across diverse interaction styles, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: TurnBench is a multi-domain benchmark for evaluating end-of-turn and interruption detection in spoken dialogue.
card.key_idea: A 30-hour triple-annotated corpus across six interaction styles paired with a standardized evaluation protocol for heterogeneous turn-taking systems.
card.evaluation: 14 systems (rule-based, commercial, and supervised) were tested on recall, FPR, and latency. VAP performed best among in-budget models.
card.limitation: Data is limited to English, dyadic, studio-recorded conversations and lacks a methodology for evaluating interruptions in full-duplex models.

slides.title: Pose-Anchored Optical Flow for Low-Latency Human Action Anticipation in Human-Robot Teaming
slides.highlight: PoseOFF uses pose-anchored optical flow to capture local motion around joints, enabling earlier human intent understanding for more responsive human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: PoseOFF improves early human action anticipation by anchoring local optical flow features to skeletal joint locations.
card.key_idea: It extracts local optical flow windows around human joints and integrates them into skeleton-based models via a lightweight CNN embedding layer, capturing fine-grained motion dynamics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on NTU RGB+D 60/120 and UCF101 using InfoGCN++, MS-G3D, and ST-GCN++. Results show improved accuracy at early observation ratios and higher AUC.
card.limitation: Less effective under severe occlusion or for actions dominated by large-scale global motion patterns.

slides.authors: Lewis de Zoete Grundy et al.

slides.title: Real-TurnTurk: A Multimodal Turkish Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal Turkish corpus and a rule-based framework for turn-taking prediction, contributing to the modeling of conversational dynamics relevant to HyECHO's focus on social perception.

card.one_liner: Introduces Real-TurnTurk, a multimodal Turkish corpus for predicting turn-taking transitions in natural dyadic conversations.
card.key_idea: A Genetic Algorithm optimizes interpretable hybrid AND-OR decision rules using 28 visual, acoustic, and linguistic features from a 2-second window preceding potential turn changes.
card.evaluation: 5-fold conversation-level cross-validation against silence thresholds and random baselines; achieved F1=57.0%, slightly exceeding the always-positive baseline (F1=50.0%).
card.limitation: Small dataset (11 conversations) with speaker imbalance, lacking listener-side visual cues and fully speaker-disjoint validation.

slides.title: Towards Actionable Surgical Team Dynamics: from Teamwork to Counterfactual Annotations
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal dataset featuring speaker diarization and annotations of group dynamics and interaction processes, supporting HyECHO's focus on social perception and team state modeling.

card.one_liner: A multimodal surgical teamwork dataset extending MM-OR with multi-level annotations and counterfactual breakdown analysis.
card.key_idea: Enriches surgical recordings with speaker diarization, bilingual transcripts, and hierarchical annotations (team, interaction, individual) plus counterfactuals to identify teamwork degradation triggers.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via three expert annotators using standardized protocols (OTAS, HMT, NOTSS, BFTQ, SYMLOG, GLIS) across 169 samples.
card.limitation: Moderate class imbalance in ratings, as recorded teams generally demonstrated acceptable performance with rare extreme scores.

slides.authors: Vincenzo Marco De Luca et al.

slides.title: Generative Action-Chunk Sampling for Adaptive Stiffness Control in Physical Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.highlight: This research proposes a framework that uses variation among sampled action chunks to adapt robot stiffness, enhancing compliance and assistance during physical human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Adaptive robot stiffness control using variation among sampled action chunks to balance assistance and compliance.
card.key_idea: A CVAE-based policy samples multiple future action chunks from an observation-conditioned prior; higher variance among samples triggers lower stiffness for human guidance.
card.evaluation: Real-world collaborative transport task (4 directions); proposed method achieved 0.95 success rate vs. 0.83 (fixed-stiffness) and 0.69 (deterministic FACTR).
card.limitation: The action-deviation signal is a proxy for uncertainty, not a calibrated probability of human intention or epistemic uncertainty.

slides.title: Why Personalization Matters: Cross-Subject Challenges in EMG-IMU-based HRI Activity Recognition
slides.highlight: This research introduces the MAGIC-HRI dataset and demonstrates that personalization is necessary for robust activity recognition in human-robot interaction, supporting the RwB goal of improving embodied social robot interactions.

card.one_liner: Personalization is essential for robust EMG-IMU activity recognition in HRI due to high inter-subject variability.
card.key_idea: Introduces MAGIC-HRI dataset (53 classes, 11 subjects) using Random Forest and a personalization strategy that injects few-shot samples from new users to improve generalization.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) and 75/25 splits using F1-score; Random Forest was the strongest baseline, showing a large generalization gap without personalization.
card.limitation: Lacks robot-in-the-loop evaluation in online settings and suffers from poor cross-subject generalization without user-specific calibration.

slides.authors: Ruan Rithelle Chagas de Faria Carminati et al.

slides.title: Simulating Cognitive Smart Freight Corridors with Agent-Based Models and Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: AGENT-BASED MODELING FOR SMART FREIGHT CORRIDORS
slides.highlight: This work uses agent-based modeling and multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive vehicle behaviors, aligning with MIMIC's focus on meso-scale simulation of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: An ABM framework using RL and MARL to optimize platoon formation and charging in smart freight corridors.
card.key_idea: A three-layer architecture (physical, cyber, decision) coupling a DQN corridor controller for lane/platoon management with MARL agents for distributed charging station pricing and priority coordination.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via three scenarios (Baseline, Assisted, Cognitive) across 5 replications. Metrics include throughput, congestion, and energy; results show Cognitive scenario's superior throughput and robustness.
card.limitation: Limited to a unidirectional network; lacks dynamic rerouting, variable speed limits, and empirical validation with real-world freight demand data.
